plan_name: MiniLinks Bookmark Manager Software Factory Orchestration Plan

structured_output.notes: Fully compliant with standard-library-only constraints (Python 3 stdlib, SQLite, vanilla HTML/CSS/JS). No external dependencies required.
structured_output.summary: Created complete MiniLinks product specification in examples/minilinks/SPEC.md documenting the exact SQLite bookmarks schema, REST API contract, static file serving with path traversal protections, create_server factory interface, testing requirements (unit test suites and 12-step smoke test), and frontend requirements.

structured_output.notes: Zero third-party dependencies; Python 3 stdlib only. Implemented thread-safe SQLite connection handling with Row factory, schema migrations with IF NOT EXISTS, case-insensitive substring searching via instr/LOWER, URL scheme/format validation, CORS preflight support, and path sanitization preventing directory traversal attacks.
structured_output.summary: Implemented the MiniLinks backend in examples/minilinks/app/server.py and examples/minilinks/app/database.py using Python 3 stdlib only, providing SQLite database operations, REST API endpoints, directory-traversal-protected static file serving, and the create_server factory running in a background daemon thread.

structured_output.notes: Zero third-party dependencies. Built using vanilla HTML5, modern CSS3 with flexbox and responsive CSS grid, and ES6+ JavaScript. All API interactions use the standard Fetch API communicating directly with /api/bookmarks. Implemented real-time and debounced search filtering, URL normalization, XSS prevention, accessible modal dialogs with keyboard navigation, and responsive card layouts.
structured_output.summary: Implemented the MiniLinks web frontend in examples/minilinks/web/index.html, style.css, and app.js with bookmark creation, debounced search filtering, edit modal, delete confirmation, responsive styling, and notification feedback.

structured_output.notes: All tests strictly utilize the Python 3 standard library (unittest, tempfile, urllib, sqlite3, threading). Tests verify API endpoints, error handling, query filtering, path traversal security, SQLite persistence across server lifecycle restarts, and end-to-end smoke verification.
structured_output.summary: Implemented comprehensive unit, integration, persistence, and smoke test suites for MiniLinks across test_api.py, test_persistence.py, and smoke_test.py.

structured_output.notes: Verified complete standard library compliance (Python 3 stdlib, SQLite, vanilla ES6+ JS, CSS3, HTML5). All REST API routes, schemas, database operations, static file serving, and error responses match SPEC.md exactly.
structured_output.summary: Performed comprehensive integration and quality verification of the MiniLinks codebase. Hardened PATCH handling for concurrent deletions, sanitized bookmark input strings in database CRUD methods, and exported MiniLinksServer in app.__init__.py.

findings.evidence: examples/minilinks/app/database.py:67-69: `WHERE instr(LOWER(COALESCE(title, \x27\x27)), ?) > 0` utilizes SQLite\x27s built-in LOWER() function, which by default only performs case-folding for standard ASCII characters (A-Z) unless SQLite is compiled with the ICU extension.
findings.recommendation: If multi-lingual Unicode search support is required in the future, register a custom Python function on the connection (e.g. `conn.create_function(\x27py_lower\x27, 1, str.lower)`) to ensure full Unicode case-insensitivity.

findings.evidence: examples/minilinks/app/database.py:13 formats timestamps using `%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ` (second resolution). Consequently, tests/test_api.py:465, tests/test_persistence.py:125, and scripts/smoke_test.py:216 utilize `time.sleep(1.05)` to guarantee that `updated_at` advances past the second boundary.
findings.recommendation: Consider using ISO 8601 timestamps with millisecond/microsecond resolution (e.g., `datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat()`) so that timestamp advancement can be validated sub-second without incurring artificial test delays.

findings.evidence: examples/minilinks/app/server.py:412 reads entire static asset files into memory via `f.read()` prior to writing to the response socket.
findings.recommendation: While suitable for lightweight text/CSS/JS assets, consider using chunked buffer streaming (e.g., 64KB chunks) if large binary or media assets are served in the future to maintain a low memory footprint.

All 12 smoke test steps, unit tests, and persistence tests are fully specified and conform strictly to Python 3 standard library and vanilla web standards with zero third-party dependencies.
